findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. For a newly started story, part or fix without a pull request, this line supplies no author, and no production code writes an `item started` event to the local event history it checks. `started_by` therefore becomes null. The removed `_starters` path previously showed the start commit's git name, so the normal pre-PR board loses a known person.
findings.title: Not done: new work keeps a visible starter before its pull request

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. This line uses the plan owner as the approver's login, although the owner and approver can differ. It also shows that owner as `approved_by` before approval. Without an Owner line, it loses recorded approval names: the adopted client's backfill stores `plan approved` in the PR time record (`src/forge/backfill.py:116–123`), while this lookup reads only local events. The existing adopted-history test expects `Plan Approver` on the archived story and part (`tests/test_board_after_upgrade.py:461,484`); those rows now have a null `approved_by`.
findings.title: Not done: approval identity names the actual approver

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The adopted-upgrade case checks the plan owner's `developer` fields here, but none of the three command-level cases asserts `approved_by_login`. The test would pass if the board gave the approver the owner's login, as it currently does. The required proof therefore cannot catch a broken login beside this person field.
findings.title: Not done: board login test covers approval identity
